thoughts.text: I am Player 0 and get the first pick. Vertex v2 is the strongest position on the board with a total of 13 pips (6-fields, 5-forest, 9-pasture), providing high production of grain, lumber, and wool, which are essential for early expansion.

I placed my first settlement at v2, which is a strong spot (9, 6, 5). Now I need to place a road. The legal edges are e1, e2, and e9. e9 leads to v9 (6, 5, 11), which is a high-value intersection and moves me toward the center of the board and potential ore (h6) and brick (h8, h16) resources.

I need to secure a source of Ore and Brick to complement the Wood, Wheat, and Wool from my first settlement at v2. Vertex 20 is the best available option for Ore, sitting on the mountain hex h6 (8), which has 5 pips. It also provides Brick from h5 (11) and Wool from h10 (12). This gives me a balanced resource base and a total of 8 pips for this settlement. While v44 has more pips (10), it would leave me without any Ore or Brick production, making it difficult to build roads, settlements, or cities later on.

I have settlements at v2 and v20. My first road e9 (v2-v9) is already placed. By placing my second road at e25 (v20-v21), I move towards connecting my two settlements via v21 and v9. This connection is strong for Longest Road and provides flexibility. Furthermore, v21 is a gateway to v31, which is a legal settlement spot adjacent to h14 (Fields 11), giving me much-needed Grain. The other options from v20, e30 and e24, lead to areas that are either blocked by other players' settlements (v13 is blocked by P3 at v8) or have less desirable resources (v24 leads to h11-2 and the desert).

It's the first turn of the game. I have settlements on a good variety of numbers (5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12) and all resource types. I have no development cards to play, so my only option is to roll the dice and start collecting resources.

I have 1 brick, 1 wool, 1 grain, and 1 ore after the first roll of 6 (which gave me 1 grain). I need lumber to expand (road/settlement), but I don't have any yet. My expansion spots (v9 and v21) require roads to reach a new settlement location. Since I have the exact resources for a development card (wool, grain, ore) and cannot build anything else this turn, buying a development card is a strong opening move. It provides potential for a Knight (robber control), Road Building, or other progress cards that can jumpstart my game.

I have only 1 brick left after buying a development card. I need lumber, wool, and grain to build a settlement at v9, which is a high-value spot (6-5-11) that I am competing for with Player 3. Since I don't have enough resources to trade for what I need and I cannot play the knight I just bought, I will end my turn.

The robber is currently on the desert (h15), so it's not blocking any of my resource production. I'll roll first to see what resources I get. If I roll a 7, I'll get to move the robber anyway. If I don't roll a 7, I can still choose to play my knight later this turn to steal a resource if I'm short on something specific for building.

I rolled a 7 and need to move the robber. I'm targeting hex h7 (fields 8) because it's a high-production (5 pips) hex occupied by Player 1, who has a strong starting position. Blocking an 8 is more effective than blocking the lower-probability hexes occupied by Player 3 (the other strong player). I'll steal from Player 1, hoping to get grain or lumber to complement my current hand of brick and wool.
I have 2 brick and 2 wool. I need lumber to build a road towards v31 or v4 to expand. I'll try to trade my surplus wool for lumber.
I have 2 brick and 2 wool. I need grain and lumber to build a settlement or road. I already tried trading wool for lumber and was rejected. I'll try trading brick for grain now.

I have 2 brick and 2 wool. I need lumber and grain to build a settlement, or grain and ore for a dev card. I already tried 1:1 trades for lumber and grain which were declined. I don't want to overpay with a 2:1 trade this early without a clear path to a settlement (I'd still need the other resource). I'm safe from a 7 (only 4 cards). I'll hold my resources and see what the next roll brings. I'll save my Knight for a more critical moment or to work towards Largest Army later.

The robber is currently on hex 5 (hills 11), which is one of my hexes (v20), but it's a low-probability hex (2 pips). I have a knight, but since the robber isn't blocking a major production source for me, I'll roll first. If I roll a 7, I can move it for free. If not, I can still play the knight later in my turn if I need to move the robber or start building towards the Largest Army.

I have 3 brick and 2 lumber. I want to expand towards a new settlement. My current settlements are at v2 and v20. I'll build a road from v2 towards v1, which is the first step toward the v0 settlement spot or the 3:1 port at v0/v5. I'll also try to trade for grain to prepare for a settlement next turn.

I have 3 bricks, 1 lumber, and 1 wool. I want to build a settlement, but I need grain and another lumber (after building a road). I'll start by playing a knight to move the robber off my settlement at v20 (h5) and hopefully steal a useful card (like grain or lumber) from Player 3, who has the most cards (6). I'll then look to build a road towards v31 to expand towards grain (h14) and ore (h9).

I'm moving the robber to hex 7 (Fields 8). This blocks Player 1's grain production, which is a high-probability hex (5 pips). Player 1 is a strong contender with two settlements close together, and blocking their grain production is a strategic move to slow them down and potentially steal a grain card, which I need for building. Although Player 3 has more cards, their most productive hexes are also ones I'm settled on (h1, h4, h6), so blocking those would hurt me as well. Hex 7 is the best balance of high-impact blocking and targeting a strong opponent without affecting my own production.

I have 4 bricks and need grain to build a settlement. I'll offer 2 bricks for 1 grain. I also need to build a road to reach a new settlement location (v31), as my current spots are blocked by the distance rule. I'll try to trade first, then build a road.

I have 2 bricks, 1 lumber, 1 wool, and 1 grain. I need to expand to get more resources. My settlement at v20 is connected to road e25, which ends at v21. From v21, I can build a road to v31 (e26) or v18 (e24). However, v18 is blocked by the distance rule because Player 3 has a settlement at v19. Therefore, v31 is my best option for future expansion. v31 is adjacent to h9 (mountains 4), h10 (pasture 12), and h14 (fields 11), which will help diversify my resource production. After building the road, I will still have 1 brick, 1 wool, and 1 grain, which I can potentially use to trade for ore or save for a future settlement.

I have already played a knight, moved the robber, traded for grain, and built a road this turn. My current hand is 1 brick, 1 wool, and 1 grain. I don't have enough resources to build anything else or buy a dev card (need ore). I'll save my resources for future turns and hope for some good rolls (5, 6, 8, 9).
I am Player 0. It is the start of my turn. I do not have any development cards to play, so I must roll the dice to proceed with my turn.

Player 1 has two settlements (v25 and v38) on hex 12 (pasture 5). Blocking this hex reduces their production by 8 pips (4 pips per settlement), which is more effective than blocking their 8-fields hex (5 pips). Player 1 also has 4 cards, making them a good target for stealing.

I have 1 brick, 3 wool, 2 grain, and 1 ore. I need 1 wool, 1 grain, and 1 ore for a development card. I also have an extra brick and two extra wool. I'll try to trade my extra wool for a lumber so I can build a road towards a new settlement spot (v31) and still have enough resources to buy a development card this turn. If the trade is rejected, I'll proceed with buying the development card anyway as it's the most efficient use of my current resources.

I have the resources (1 wool, 1 grain, 1 ore) to buy a development card. I currently lack the lumber needed for roads or settlements, and my previous trade offer for lumber was rejected. Buying a development card is a strong alternative that could provide a Knight for board control, a Victory Point, or a progress card like Road Building or Year of Plenty which would help me expand.

I have 1 brick, 1 wool, and 1 grain after buying a development card. I've already tried to trade wool for lumber, which was declined by all players. I have no other productive actions to take this turn as I lack the resources for further building and cannot play the knight I just bought. My current settlements are well-positioned for resource production (6, 8, 5, 9, 11), so I will wait for future rolls to accumulate resources for expansion toward v31 or v32.

I have 4 cards and am not currently blocked by the robber (the robber is on h18, but my 6 is on h1). There is no risk of discarding if I roll a 7. Playing the knight before rolling is only beneficial if I am blocked or if I want to steal a card before someone potentially discards it (but no one has more than 7 cards). Rolling first provides more information.

Player 1 currently has the most cards (5) and is settled on hex h12 twice (at v25 and v38). Hex h12 is a 5 (4 pips), so blocking it effectively stops 8 pips of production for Player 1, which is their strongest resource source. Stealing from Player 1 also gives me a good chance of obtaining lumber or brick, which I need for expansion.

I have 1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, and 2 grain. To expand, I need to build a road first because my current settlements (v2 and v20) are only 1 edge away from any potential new settlement spot. Building a road on e39 (v21-v32) will lead me toward v32, which is a valid settlement location (2 edges away from v20 and v19). v32 produces grain, lumber, and ore (h14, h13, h9), which are resources I need. I'll start by building the road.

I have 1 wool and 2 grain after building a road this turn. I cannot build a settlement or city, or buy a dev card with my current resources. I have a knight card, but I've already moved the robber this turn by rolling a 7. I'll save the knight for a future turn to either move the robber off my productive hexes (like the 6 or 8) or to secure Largest Army later. Proposing a trade for brick or lumber might be difficult since I only have grain to offer and I've already used some resources this turn. I'll end my turn and wait for more production.

I currently have 5 cards (1 brick, 1 wool, 3 grain), so I'm safe from a 7 roll. My settlements (v2 and v20) are not blocked by the robber, which is currently on h12 (affecting Player 1). There is no immediate advantage to playing the knight before rolling, as I'd rather see the outcome of the roll first. If I roll a 7, I'll move the robber for free. If not, I can still play the knight later this turn if I need to steal a specific resource (like lumber or ore) to build or buy a development card.
I need one lumber to build a settlement at v31. I have excess grain. I'll try to trade grain for lumber with any player.

I have 1 brick, 1 wool, and 3 grain. I need 1 lumber to build a settlement at v31 (which I have a road to). I already tried a 1:1 trade for lumber which was rejected. I will now try a more generous 2:1 trade (2 grain for 1 lumber) to see if anyone is willing to trade. If this fails, I still have a knight I can play to steal a card, or I can try other trades. P3 is a good target for lumber since they have settlements on forest hexes (h2 and h4).

I have 1 brick, 1 wool, and 3 grain. I need 1 lumber to build a settlement at v31, which is already connected to my road network (e39). I've already tried trading 2 grain for 1 lumber, but all players declined. My best chance to get the lumber this turn is to play my knight and steal a card from Player 3, who has 6 cards and settlements on forest hexes (h2 and h13). Playing the knight will also move the robber from h12 (blocking Player 1) to a hex that blocks Player 3 (like h8 or h2). According to the rules and the provided schema, I can play one dev card per turn. After playing the knight, I hope to receive a lumber and then build my settlement.

I am moving the robber to hex h8 (Hills 10). This hex is occupied by both Player 3 and Player 1. Player 3 is currently a significant threat with the most roads and a strong board presence, and Player 1 is also doing well. Blocking a brick-producing hex (Hills) will slow down their expansion, as both likely need brick for roads and settlements. I'll steal from Player 3 since they have the most cards (6) and are a primary competitor.

P3 has more cards (6) compared to P1 (5). Both gained a brick on the last roll (10) because they both have settlements on hex 8. P3 also gained lumber on turn 19, and I am looking for lumber to build a settlement or road. P3 seems like the more lucrative target and a slightly stronger opponent at the moment.

I have already played a Knight this turn. According to the rules 'buy/play one dev card per turn', I have likely used my development card action for this turn and cannot buy another. I have also attempted multiple trades for lumber (1 grain, 2 grain, 1 ore) which were all declined by the other players. Since I lack the lumber for a settlement or road, and do not have enough resources for a city or a 4:1 bank trade, I will end my turn.
I have 7 cards, which is exactly the limit before needing to discard on a 7. I have no playable development cards, so my only option is to roll the dice and proceed with my turn.

I have the resources (1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain) to build a settlement at v31, which is my only currently available legal settlement site. This will increase my VP to 3 and provide additional production from h9 (mountains 4), h10 (pasture 12), and h14 (fields 11).
I have 3 grain and 1 ore. I need 1 wool to buy a development card. I'm checking if anyone is willing to trade wool for my excess grain.

I have 3 grain and 1 ore. I need 1 wool to buy a development card. I'll offer 2 grain for 1 wool to see if anyone is interested, especially since P2 has 8 cards and might want to reduce their hand size.

I have exactly the resources for a development card (1 wool, 1 grain, 1 ore). Since I cannot build anything else and P3 is pulling ahead, getting a dev card for potential knights or VPs is the best move.
I have no resources left after buying a development card and building a settlement this turn. I cannot play the knight I just bought until my next turn. Therefore, I must end my turn.

I have 0 cards and the robber is currently blocking my best source of Ore (h6, 8). P3 is the leader with 5 VP and just stole from me. By playing the knight before rolling, I can unblock my production (in case an 8 is rolled), move the robber to a hex that hinders P3, and steal a card to jumpstart my turn.

P3 is the current leader (tied with me at 5 VP) and has a city on h2 (Forest 4). Blocking h2 targets P3's city, which is more effective than blocking their settlements on h8 or h9, and it doesn't hurt my own production (unlike h1 or h4). P3 also has 6 cards, making them a good target for stealing. P1 has more cards (7), but P3 is the primary threat to win.
P3 is currently tied with me at 5 VP and holds the Longest Road. They also have more cards (6) than P2 (4), making them a higher priority target to slow down.

I have already played a knight this turn to move the robber off hex 6 (mountains 8) to hex 2 (forest 4), which affects P2 and P3. I've also stolen a grain from P3. Now I need to roll the dice to proceed with my turn.

P3 is currently tied with me at 5 VP and holds the Longest Road, making them the primary threat. I need to move the robber from h2 (where I just placed it with a knight) because I rolled a 7. I'll move it to h8 (hills 10), which blocks P3's settlement at v19 and also hits P1 at v25. This hex is ideal because I don't have any settlements adjacent to it, so I won't be blocking my own production, unlike other P3-adjacent hexes like h1, h4, h5, and h9.

P3 is currently tied with me at 5 VP and holds the Longest Road, making them my primary competitor. Although P1 has more cards (7), P3's position is stronger, so I will steal from them again to minimize their resources and slow their progress.

I have 2 grain and no other resources. I cannot build anything or buy a development card. While I could try to trade, with only 2 grain and no immediate path to a settlement or city, it's unlikely I'll get a beneficial trade this turn. I already have Largest Army and 5 VP, putting me in a decent position. I will end my turn and wait for more production.
I have no playable development cards, so I cannot play a knight before rolling. I must roll the dice to start my turn.

P3 is my main competitor, tied with me at 5 VP. P3 has a city on hex 2 (Forest 4), which is a 3-pip hex. Blocking this hex hurts P3's production more than any other hex where I am not also present. Hexes 1, 4, 5, and 9 all have P3 buildings but also contain my own settlements, so blocking them would be counter-productive. Hex 8 is another option (P3 settlement on a 3-pip hex), but blocking a city on hex 2 is more effective. I'll steal from P3 to reduce their 7-card hand and hopefully gain a resource I need (brick, lumber, or wool).

P3 is currently tied with me for the lead (5 VP) and holds the Longest Road. They also have more cards (7) than P2 (5), making them the more significant threat and a better target for a steal, especially after they stole from me last turn.

I have 1 lumber, 2 grain, and 1 ore. I need 1 wool to buy a development card, which is my best path forward to secure my lead and potentially get a victory point or maintain Largest Army. Player 1 has the best wool production (h12, pasture 5) with two settlements there (v25, v38). Player 1 also has grain production (h7, fields 8), but they might be willing to trade. I'll propose a trade of 1 grain for 1 wool to everyone, but I'm primarily targeting Player 1.

I need wool to buy a development card or to save for a settlement. I have lumber, grain, and ore. I already tried trading grain for wool and everyone declined. P1 has 4 cards and might need lumber for a road or settlement.
I have 2 grain and 1 ore. I need 2 more ore for a city or 1 wool for a dev card. Since my previous wool trades were rejected, I'll try to get ore to move toward a city on v2 (6, 9, 5).

I have 1 lumber, 2 grain, and 1 ore. I cannot build a city (needs 3 ore, 2 grain), a settlement (needs 1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain), or buy a dev card (needs 1 ore, 1 wool, 1 grain). I have already reached the limit of 3 trade proposals this turn, and I do not have enough resources for a 4:1 bank trade. Therefore, I must end my turn.

I have 9 cards, so there's a risk of rolling a 7 and discarding. However, I don't have any playable knights to move the robber before rolling. My current goal is to accumulate resources for a city or settlement. I have a surplus of grain (5) and some brick (2), lumber (1), and ore (1). I'll roll and then see if I can trade for what I need.

I have 10 cards and need to spend them to avoid losing half on a 7. I have a surplus of grain (5) and need one more ore to build a city or one wool to buy a dev card. A city at vertex 2 would be a huge boost to my production (9, 6, 5). I'll try to trade for the ore first.

I have 2 brick, 1 lumber, 5 grain, and 2 ore. I need one more ore to build a city at vertex 2, which is my most productive settlement (on hexes 9, 6, and 5). Since my previous trade offer of 2 grain for 1 ore was declined by all players, I will use a bank trade to get the final ore I need. I have 5 grain, so I can trade 4 grain for 1 ore. This will leave me with 1 grain and 3 ore, allowing me to build the city next. Although it's inefficient, the city provides a significant boost to my production and an extra victory point.

I have 3 ore and 1 grain, and I need one more grain to build a city (total 3 ore, 2 grain). I also have 2 brick and 1 lumber. I will try to trade 1 brick for 1 grain with the other players to see if I can get the resources for a city this turn. If this fails, I might consider building a road to avoid losing cards to a 7, but getting the city is a priority for VP and production.

I have 1 grain and 3 ore, but I need 2 grain and 3 ore to build a city. I already tried to trade 1 brick for 1 grain and was rejected. I'll try a more generous offer of 1 brick and 1 lumber for 1 grain to see if anyone is willing to trade. If I get the grain, I can build a city at vertex 2, which has excellent numbers (9, 6, 5).

I need one more grain to build a city (costing 2 grain and 3 ore). I currently have 1 grain and 3 ore. By trading 1 brick and 1 lumber for 1 grain, I will have the resources to upgrade one of my settlements to a city. I am choosing to trade with Player 1 because they only have 2 VP, whereas Player 3 is the current leader with 6 VP and the Longest Road.

I have 1 brick, 2 grain, and 3 ore. A city costs 2 grain and 3 ore. I have a settlement at vertex 2, which is a high-production spot (pips: 5, 4, 4 on resources grain, wool, and lumber). Upgrading this settlement to a city will increase my VP from 5 to 6 and double my production on those hexes. I've already traded this turn to get the necessary grain, so I will now build the city.

I have already upgraded my settlement at vertex 2 to a city this turn, which used up most of my resources. I currently have only 1 brick left and no playable development cards. I have already attempted to trade my brick for other resources and was declined by all players. Therefore, I have no further actions I can take this turn.

I have no playable development cards (specifically no knights) to use before rolling. I need to roll to gain resources and progress towards my next city or settlement. P3 is currently my main competitor with 6 points, but I hold the Largest Army.

I have 2 brick, 1 grain, and 1 ore. I need 1 wool to buy a development card (which costs 1 wool, 1 grain, 1 ore). Looking at the board, Player 1 is the only other player with access to a pasture (h12, number 5). I will propose a trade of 1 brick for 1 wool to Player 1, or anyone else who might have wool from a previous roll or trade.

I have 2 brick, 1 grain, and 1 ore. I need wool to buy a development card or lumber to build a road. I already tried trading 1 brick for 1 wool, but everyone declined. Since P3 just gained 2 brick and P1 already has brick production, it's unlikely they want more brick. P2 doesn't have wool production. I'll try one more trade offering 2 bricks for 1 wool to see if P1 (the only wool producer) is interested. If this fails, I will end my turn and wait for my strong production numbers (5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12) to give me the resources I need.

I have 1 wool, 1 grain, and 1 ore, which is the exact cost of a development card. I currently have 6 VP and the Largest Army (3 knights played). Buying a development card is the best move here to either get a Victory Point card, another Knight to secure my lead, or a useful progress card like Road Building or Year of Plenty. I don't have enough resources for a settlement or a city, and trading for them with only 3 cards in hand is unlikely to be successful.

I have no resources left in my hand after trading for wool and buying a development card (Road Building). Since the development card was bought this turn, I cannot play it. I have no other possible actions, so I must end my turn.

I need to roll the dice to start my turn. I don't have a knight to play before rolling. My goal is to gather more resources to build settlements or cities, as I'm currently tied for the lead with Player 3 at 6 VP.

I need wool to build a settlement or buy a dev card. I have 2 lumber and 1 brick, so I can afford to trade one lumber. P1 has 10 cards and production on a wool hex (h12), so they are a likely trade partner. If I get the wool, I can use my road_building card to expand towards the wool port (v6) or the 3:1 port (v0) and build a settlement.

I am currently at 6 VP, tied with Player 3. I have a Road Building card and enough resources to build a settlement if I can acquire one wool. My current settlements/cities (v2, v20, v31) are somewhat boxed in, so I need to expand. Using Road Building to move from v31 toward v41 seems like a good plan, as v41 is a legal settlement spot (neighbors v32, v42, v44 are all vacant and not adjacent to any existing buildings). Before using the Road Building card, I'll try to trade for the wool I need for a settlement. I'll offer 1 ore for 1 wool, as ore is valuable for cities and might entice a trade more than the lumber I offered previously.

I need wool to build a settlement or a dev card. Player 2 gained wool on turn 42 (roll of 10). I have plenty of ore and lumber. If I get the wool, I can use my Road Building card to reach a new settlement spot (v50) and build it this turn, or at least be ready for it. v50 is a good spot because it's on a 6 (grain) and 10 (wool).

I have 6 VP, tied with Player 3 for the lead. I need to expand to secure more resources, especially wool and grain, to build settlements and cities. Player 1 is currently at v38 and has a road to v42, making them a threat to the high-yield spot at v44 (Grain 6/11, Wool 10). By playing my Road Building card now, I can reach v44 before Player 1. I will place my first two roads towards v44 (via v32 and v41) and then use my remaining brick and lumber to build a third road to reach the vertex. This also helps me work toward the Longest Road, which Player 3 currently holds with 7 segments.

I'm using my Road Building development card to expand towards a new settlement location. My city at v2 is adjacent to some good numbers (9, 6, 5), and building towards v0 (h0: 9, h1: 6) with its 3:1 port is a strong move. The path from v2 to v0 is e1 then e0. This first move places the road on e1.

I have already placed the first of my two free roads from the Road Building development card on edge e1 (v1-v2), which connects to my city at v2. Now I need to place the second road. Looking at the legal options provided (e0, e10, e24, e30, e40, e44), edge e0 (v0-v1) is the most strategic choice. It continues my road from v1 to v0. Vertex v0 is a 3:1 port on hex h0 (Pasture 9), and it is a legal settlement spot (distance 2 from my city at v2). Securing a 3:1 port will be crucial for my flexibility in the mid-to-late game, especially since I'm currently struggling to trade for wool. Other options like e40 or e24 lead to blocked or less desirable locations.

I have 1 brick, 2 lumber, 1 grain, and 2 ore. I need 1 wool to build a settlement at v0, which is the only legal settlement site currently reachable. I've already used my three trade attempts this turn and they were all rejected. I cannot bank trade (no 4-of-a-kind). While I could build a road, it's better to save the brick and lumber for the settlement at v0 once I acquire wool. I am safe from a 7 roll (6 cards).

I currently have 6 VP and the Largest Army. My hand contains 1 brick, 2 lumber, 1 grain, and 2 ore. I have no playable development cards (specifically no knights to move the robber before rolling). The robber is currently on one of my best hexes (h1, fields 6), but I must roll to proceed with my turn.

I have 1 brick, 2 lumber, 1 grain, and 2 ore. I want to build a city (needs 3 ore, 2 grain) or buy a dev card (needs 1 wool, 1 grain, 1 ore). I have plenty of lumber and a brick. I'll try to trade my surplus lumber for grain or wool. P1, P2, and P3 all recently received grain (P1 and P3 on turn 47, P2 on turn 48). I'll start by proposing a trade for grain.

I have 1 brick, 2 lumber, 1 grain, and 2 ore. I need 1 wool to build a settlement at v0, which is on a pasture hex (h0, number 9). I've already tried trading lumber for wool, but it was declined. I'll offer a more attractive trade: 1 lumber and 1 ore for 1 wool. If this is accepted, I will have the resources (1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain) to build a settlement at v0, bringing me to 7 VP.

I am currently at 6 VP (1 city, 2 settlements, and Largest Army). I have the resources (1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain) to build a settlement at v0, which is a legal site and connects to my road network at e0. Building at v0 will increase my VP to 7 and grant me access to the 3:1 port at e5. Although there was a trade earlier in the turn, I will rely on the 'Your hand' status which explicitly states I have the necessary resources.

I have 7 VP and only 1 ore in my hand after building a settlement at v0. I cannot build anything else or buy a development card this turn, as I lack the necessary resources and have no more cards to trade. P3 is the closest competitor with 6 VP and the Longest Road. I will end my turn.

I currently have 7 VP and the Largest Army. My goal is to reach 10 VP. I have 1 brick and 2 ore in my hand, and the robber is currently blocking my ore production on hex 6 (mountains 8). I don't have any playable development cards (specifically knights) to move the robber before rolling, so my only option is to roll the dice and proceed with my turn.

I have 1 brick, 2 grain, and 2 ore. To build a city, I need 2 grain and 3 ore. I am one ore short, but I have a brick I can trade. I'll propose a trade of 1 brick for 1 ore. If accepted, I will have the 2 grain and 3 ore necessary to upgrade one of my settlements (v20 or v31) to a city, which will bring me to 8 VP. v20 is a better long-term choice for ore production (h6 is an 8), though it's currently blocked by the robber. v31 is also a good option. I'll start by trying to get the resource I need.

I have 1 brick, 2 grain, and 2 ore. To build a city, I need 3 ore and 2 grain. I already attempted to trade my brick for an ore, but all players declined. I cannot build a road, settlement, or buy a dev card with my current resources (missing lumber and wool). I have a 3:1 port, but I don't have 3 of any single resource to use it. Ending my turn is the safest move to avoid over-trading and to stay under the 7-card limit, while waiting for production from my settlements and city.

I am currently at 7 VP and need 3 more to win. I have 4 grain and 2 ore, so I'm close to being able to build another city (needs 3 ore, 2 grain). I don't have any playable development cards (like a Knight) to move the robber off my ore hex (h6) before rolling, so my only option is to roll the dice and see what resources I get.

I have 7 VP (City v2: 2, Settlement v0: 1, Settlement v20: 1, Settlement v31: 1, Largest Army: 2). I have 1 brick, 6 grain, and 2 ore. I have a 3:1 port at v0. I need 3 more VP to win. A city upgrade is a guaranteed 1 VP. I will trade 3 grain for 1 ore using my 3:1 port, which will give me the 3 ore and 2 grain needed for a city. I'll then build the city on v20 because it's on an 8 (mountains), which is high-production once the robber moves.
